- The user explicitly says "worktree" (e.g., "start a worktree", "work in a worktree", "create a worktree", "use a worktree")
- CLAUDE.md or memory instructions direct you to work in a worktree for the current task

## When NOT to Use

- The user asks to create a branch, switch branches, or work on a different branch — use git commands instead
- The user asks to fix a bug or work on a feature — use normal git workflow unless worktrees are explicitly requested by the user or project instructions
- Never use this tool unless "worktree" is explicitly mentioned by the user or in CLAUDE.md / memory instructions

## Requirements

- Must be in a git repository, OR have WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks configured in settings.json
- Must not already be in a worktree session when creating a new worktree (`name`); switching into another existing worktree via `path` is allowed

## Behavior

- In a git repository: creates a new git worktree inside `.claude/worktrees/` on a new branch. The base ref is governed by the `worktree.baseRef` setting: `fresh` (default) branches from origin/<default-branch>; `head` branches from your current local HEAD
- Outside a git repository: delegates to WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks for VCS-agnostic isolation
- Switches the session's working directory to the new worktree
- Use ExitWorktree to leave the worktree mid-session (keep or remove). On session exit, if still in the worktree, the user will be prompted to keep or remove it

## Entering an existing worktree

Pass `path` instead of `name` to switch the session into a worktree that already exists (e.g., one you just created with `git worktree add`). On first entry from the launch directory, the path must appear in `git worktree list` for the repository that owns it — the current repository or, in a multi-repo workspace, a repository nested inside it; paths registered by neither are rejected. ExitWorktree will not remove a worktree entered this way; use `action: "keep"` to return to the original directory.

Switching with `path` also works when the session is already in a worktree (the previous worktree is left on disk, untouched, and only the new one is tracked for exit-time cleanup), and from agents whose working directory was pinned at launch (subagent isolation or explicit cwd). In both cases the target must be a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` of the same repository, and from a pinned agent the switch only affects this agent, not the parent session. After a further switch, previously-visited worktrees are no longer writable — re-issue EnterWorktree with `path` to return to one.

## Parameters

- `name` (optional): A name for a new worktree. If neither `name` nor `path` is provided, a random name is generated.
- `path` (optional): Path to an existing worktree to enter instead of creating one — of the current repository, or (on first entry from the launch directory) of a repository nested inside it. Mutually exclusive with `name`.

name.description: Optional name for a new worktree. Each "/"-separated segment may contain only letters, digits, dots, underscores, and dashes; max 64 chars total. A random name is generated if not provided. Mutually exclusive with `path`.

path.description: Path to an existing worktree to switch into instead of creating a new one. Must appear in `git worktree list` for the current repo — or, on first entry from the launch directory, for a repo nested inside it (multi-repo workspace). Mutually exclusive with `name`.

tools.name: ExitWorktree
tools.description:
Exit a worktree session created by EnterWorktree and return the session to the original working directory.

## Scope

This tool ONLY operates on worktrees created by EnterWorktree in this session. It will NOT touch:
- Worktrees you created manually with `git worktree add`
- Worktrees from a previous session (even if created by EnterWorktree then)
- The directory you're in if EnterWorktree was never called

If called outside an EnterWorktree session, the tool is a **no-op**: it reports that no worktree session is active and takes no action. Filesystem state is unchanged.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly asks to "exit the worktree", "leave the worktree", "go back", or otherwise end the worktree session
- Do NOT call this proactively — only when the user asks

## Parameters

- `action` (required): `"keep"` or `"remove"`
  - `"keep"` — leave the worktree directory and branch intact on disk. Use this if the user wants to come back to the work later, or if there are changes to preserve.
  - `"remove"` — delete the worktree directory and its branch. Use this for a clean exit when the work is done or abandoned.
- `discard_changes` (optional, default false): only meaningful with `action: "remove"`. If the worktree has uncommitted files or commits not on the original branch, the tool will REFUSE to remove it unless this is set to `true`. If the tool returns an error listing changes, confirm with the user before re-invoking with `discard_changes: true`.

## Behavior

- Restores the session's working directory to where it was before EnterWorktree
- Clears CWD-dependent caches (system prompt sections, memory files, plans directory) so the session state reflects the original directory
- If a tmux session was attached to the worktree: killed on `remove`, left running on `keep` (its name is returned so the user can reattach)
- Once exited, EnterWorktree can be called again to create a fresh worktree

tools.name: NotebookEdit
tools.description:
Replaces, inserts, or deletes a single cell in a Jupyter notebook (.ipynb file).

Usage:

Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.

tools.name: SendMessage
tools.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: WebFetch
tools.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

DeepWiki MCP provides AI-powered documentation for GitHub repositories.

- read_wiki_structure: Get a list of documentation topics for a repository
- read_wiki_contents: View full documentation about a repository
- ask_wiki_question: Ask any question about a repository's codebase and get an AI-powered answer from its wiki
- list_wiki_repos: List the repositories that have a DeepWiki index (private mode only)
- generate_wiki: Generate a codebase wiki for a repository — only use when explicitly requested by the user (private mode only)
- devin_automation_manage: Manage Devin automations — list, get, create, update, delete, or fetch the trigger event schemas (private mode only)
- devin_billing_tag_manage: Manage Devin billing tags (groupings of Devin sessions for usage tracking) — list, get, create, assign sessions, look up session tags (private mode only)
- devin_blueprint_test: Test a candidate blueprint YAML in an authoring VM: start → run initialize → fix → run initialize again (clean VM) → run maintenance → then persist with update_environment_config (private mode only)
- devin_campaign_manage: Read and publish a bot's campaign documents (plan, readings, status) — get, update, validate (private mode only)
- devin_code_scan_manage: Manage Devin code scans, sometimes referred to as 'security scans' or 'Devin Security Swarm' — list scans, list findings, list profiles, get a profile, create a scan, remediate a finding (private mode only)
- devin_knowledge_manage: Manage Devin knowledge notes and suggestions — list, search, get, create, update, delete notes, view folder structure, list/view/dismiss knowledge suggestions (private mode only)
- devin_mcp_server_manage: Manage org MCP server installations — install (marketplace or custom), update, enable, disable, delete (private mode only)
- devin_oncall_manage: Devin Oncall operations — create and manage Oncall responders (alert, bug report and support request triage), get an Oncall report's current responder membership, page through a responder's open issues, and ingest a dashboard into Oncall knowledge (private mode only)
- devin_playbook_manage: Manage Devin playbooks — list, get, create, update, delete (private mode only)
- devin_review_manage: Trigger a Devin Review for a pull request, fetch the latest review status, or fetch a completed review's findings (private mode only)
- devin_schedule_manage: Manage scheduled Devin sessions — list, get, create, update, delete (private mode only)
- devin_session_create: Create one or more child Devin sessions (private mode only)
- devin_session_interact: Manage a Devin session — get status (one or many sessions, optionally with a short AI summary of each), send messages, sleep/terminate/archive/unarchive, read messages & attachments, manage tags (private mode only)
- devin_session_events: Inspect session events — list summaries, fetch full details, or search event contents (private mode only)
- devin_session_search: Search and filter Devin sessions (private mode only)
- devin_session_insights: Per-session cost, message counts and AI analysis (issues, action items, classification) — list, get, generate (private mode only)
- devin_user_list: List the organization's users by membership kind (direct members or IdP-group members) (private mode only)
- devin_list_integrations: List all native integrations and MCP servers with their status and settings URLs (private mode only)
- devin_find_setting: Find Devin webapp settings pages and deep-link URLs for them (private mode only)

1	# Repository Guidelines
2	
3	## Scope and authority
4	
5	`dsh-agent-team` is an opt-in, externally installable Cordis bundle for DeepSeek Harness. It adds a single-host Agent Team without modifying the Harness repository, the agent loop, or shipped defaults.
6	
7	Read [`docs/README.md`](docs/README.md) first — it is the maintained documentation index.
8	
9	Use this authority order:
10	
11	1. **Current behavior:** source and tests under `packages/`. When prose disagrees with code, code wins.
12	2. **Maintained engineering guidance:** `docs/`. Update it when a code or workflow change invalidates it; it must not define behavior that the code does not implement.
13	3. **Harness contract:** `../deepseek-harness/docs/`, its applicable `AGENTS.md`, and the corresponding Harness source/tests.
14	4. **Work history:** `.scratch/` — active work items and archived design, research, tickets, prototypes, and validation evidence. It is not an implementation or API authority; its own [`AGENTS.md`](.scratch/AGENTS.md) governs how to work there, and the [`README.md`](.scratch/README.md) indexes it. Verify relevant history against code, tests, and the Harness contract.
15	
16	Keep production code self-explanatory through clear names, types, and structure. Comments explain only non-obvious constraints, ownership, or reasons; they are not the sole definition of current behavior. The `check:comments` row in [`docs/development/start-and-checks.md`](docs/development/start-and-checks.md) holds the per-scope budget and the rules a comment's references must satisfy.
17	
18	When deleting comments in bulk, a green test suite proves nothing about the change. Tests assert behavior; comments are text. Measure the edit itself instead: audit the diff so every removed line is a comment or a blank line, and treat any removed code line as a failure. Delete whole comment blocks rather than merged line ranges — a merged range swallows the code between two comments — and never normalize whitespace outside the lines you removed. This applies to any sweep over comments, including one driven by a subagent report: reports carry line numbers that drift, so verify each cited range against the current file before acting on it.
19	
20	## Reading guidance
21	
22	- Use the `docs/architecture/` pages for package ownership, Host authority, Remote, preset, and Client boundaries — not before every edit, only when a change crosses those boundaries: [`package-ownership.md`](docs/architecture/package-ownership.md), [`host-authority.md`](docs/architecture/host-authority.md), [`tools-and-preset.md`](docs/architecture/tools-and-preset.md), [`client-and-remote.md`](docs/architecture/client-and-remote.md), [`workspace-session-storage.md`](docs/architecture/workspace-session-storage.md).
23	- Use [`docs/harness-navigation.md`](docs/harness-navigation.md) for cross-repository routes when a change consumes a Harness capability.
24	- Treat `.scratch/` as background context, not as a specification to implement blindly. New cross-session work belongs in one `.scratch/active/<work>/` directory; close it into the archive only after durable conclusions have moved to maintained documents.
25	
26	## Architecture guardrails
27	
28	- `packages/agent-team` is the only Team authority. Its append-only operation ledger is the durable source of Team facts; projections, tools, commands, Remote, and UI do not maintain parallel authority.
29	- `packages/tool-agent-team` provides the seven model-facing Team tools only through the explicit `team-member` preset. The Web Client is the only Human Team control surface; do not restore a slash-command adapter.
30	- Team is an external plugin. Do not modify `../deepseek-harness`, its agent loop, or shipped defaults for ordinary Team work. If a public Harness extension point is insufficient, record the limitation and decide whether to implement a Team-owned plugin or change the design.
31	- Typed Remote declarations are the input; Typert artifacts are generated. Never hand-edit `packages/agent-team/lib/typert.*`.
32	- The Client uses public Harness plugin and slot APIs. Mount the generated Remote, wait for `remote.agentTeam`, and use `ctx.slots.inject()` when a declaration may not exist yet; `dsh.client.inject` is not an activation-order guarantee.
33	- A slot parent’s `children` declaration is its render authority. Do not copy private shipped UI or redeclare `sidebar.workspaces.directoryFlow` from the Team workspace shadow; live duplicate child declarations are rejected by Harness SlotCore, regardless of priority.
34	- Keep durable UI mutations non-optimistic. Authorization, membership, revisions, idempotency, and stable branded refs are enforced by the Host.
35	- Keep Team tools/guidance inside the isolated Team preset. Ordinary Sessions must not acquire Team behavior accidentally.
36	
37	## Code and documentation conventions
38	
39	- Use ESM, strict TypeScript, `.ts`/`.tsx` local imports, existing package names, and existing branded domain types.
40	- Keep one authoritative formatter/projection per domain concept. Do not add speculative registries, compatibility layers, fallback authorities, or duplicate stores.
41	- Do not hand-edit generated `tsconfig*.json` path facades. Change `scripts/sync-paths.mjs` and regenerate.
42	- Update the affected maintained document, package README, and tests when a non-trivial change alters a public contract or workflow. Do not update archived `.scratch/` material merely to make it agree with new code.
43	- Follow [`docs/AGENTS.md`](docs/AGENTS.md) when editing or adding maintained documents — routing branches and the maintenance discipline live there.
44	- For visible UI changes, run the applicable component checks and `npm run test:browser`, inspect the new `artifacts/browser/` screenshots at desktop and 390×844, and verify keyboard/focus, dialog/menu accessibility, loading/error/empty states, and ordinary DSH restoration. Keep only a small, human-approved milestone set under `.scratch/archive/.../validation/`; routine screenshots stay ignored.
45	- Write each commit message as one Conventional Commits subject line: `type: lowercase imperative summary` (`feat`, `fix`, `chore`, `refactor`, `test`, `perf`, `docs`), with no body. Match the existing `git log` style.
46	- Do not commit credentials, temporary profiles, browser overlays, generated test files, browser artifacts, or build residue.
47	
48	## Checks
49	
50	Run the narrowest applicable check, then escalate for the changed surface. The exact workflow is in [`docs/development/start-and-checks.md`](docs/development/start-and-checks.md).
51	
52	`npm run test:browser` is required for changes that can affect the assembled Web bundle, Client loading, slot takeover, Remote activation, or visible UI. It uses the adjacent Harness checkout and a temporary profile; it does not modify the Harness repository permanently.
53	
54	Release cadence is batched: between releases the operator daily-drives a locally linked build as a lightweight acceptance channel, so choose the narrowest applicable check per change instead of demanding full acceptance for every small fix. When asking the operator to preview or accept a change, point them at the dev profile (`dsh web --profile web-dev`); the default `web` profile stays on the published stable release. See "Profile 模式与发布节奏" in [`docs/development/environments-and-install.md`](docs/development/environments-and-install.md).
55	
56	## Further reading
57	
58	- Domain and Host behavior: `packages/agent-team/src/`, its tests, and `docs/architecture/README.md`.
59	- Tools and preset: `packages/tool-agent-team/`, `packages/agent-team/preset/`, and the matching Harness subsystem docs.
60	- Client or UI: `packages/client-agent-team/src/client/`, `docs/architecture/README.md`, and `docs/harness-navigation.md`; consult the relevant `.scratch/archive/` work history only when needed, and verify all behavior in code and tests.
61

2	
3	This directory holds the repository's maintained engineering documentation. The root `AGENTS.md` keeps rules every task must know; this file only governs how to work here — routing a change to the document that owns its facts, and the discipline that keeps the set truthful.
4	
5	## Routing
6	
7	A change that invalidates a documented fact updates the owning document in the same change:
8	
9	| Change touches | Update |
10	| --- | --- |

18	| A model-facing tool contract, or a rule shared by every tool | [`team-collaboration/tools.md`](team-collaboration/tools.md) |
19	| Attention, Inbox, mentions, or how a Message is rendered | [`team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.md`](team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.md) |
20	| Mutation fences, the Human Remote boundary, or the Member context boundary | [`team-collaboration/boundaries.md`](team-collaboration/boundaries.md) |
21	| Member memory, context pressure ownership, Agent notifications, or assembled acceptance | [`team-collaboration/memory-and-context.md`](team-collaboration/memory-and-context.md) |

26	| The sidebar browser or the Inbox surface | [`frontend-design/sidebar-browser.md`](frontend-design/sidebar-browser.md) |
27	| Refresh semantics, copy, accessibility, or evolution | [`frontend-design/refresh-copy-accessibility.md`](frontend-design/refresh-copy-accessibility.md) |
28	| Setup, the verification gradient, or which check a change needs | [`development/start-and-checks.md`](development/start-and-checks.md) |
29	| Browser evidence, generated files, package seams, or adding a Host operation | [`development/generated-and-seams.md`](development/generated-and-seams.md) |
30	| Sandbox/CI environments, external installation, or release cadence | [`development/environments-and-install.md`](development/environments-and-install.md) |
31	| Ledger storage routing, notification regression, or a delivery checklist | [`development/storage-and-delivery.md`](development/storage-and-delivery.md) |
32	| Publishing a release, release gates, or release material | [`release-runbook.md`](release-runbook.md) |
33	| DSH certification, `peerDependencies`, or installation checks | [`dsh-release-compatibility.md`](dsh-release-compatibility.md) |
34	| Cross-repository lookup | [`harness-navigation.md`](harness-navigation.md) |
35	| User-visible behavior | [`../CHANGELOG.md`](../CHANGELOG.md) |
36	
37	The full index and Where to start paths are in [`README.md`](README.md).
38	
39	## Maintenance discipline
40	
41	- Source and tests define implementation behavior. When prose conflicts with code, fix the documentation — never record behavior the code does not implement.
42	- One fact has one maintained home; cross-link between documents instead of duplicating the fact.
43	- Maintained docs ship as bilingual pairs: change `foo.zh.md` in the same change as `foo.md`, translating prose while keeping domain entity names in English (Agent, Member, Session, Workspace, Project, Thread, Task, Claim, preset, Remote). A Chinese rendering is correct only when it names a different concept: `membership` renders as 成员关系, but a Member entity is always Member. Interface labels keep their natural Chinese — the `项目 · …` chip stays as-is.
44	- Both sides of a pair state the same rules and carry the same outline — the same headings at the same levels, in the same order, which `check:docs` decides. How a rule is rendered is the translator's call and is deliberately not compared: a list in one half and a table or prose in the other is legal. Implementation naming — a file, symbol, storage key, or CSS value — may appear on only one side.
45	- A new maintained document gets an index row and a Where to start path in both `README.md` and `README.zh.md` in the same change.
46	- Write uncertain facts as `> TODO:` instead of guessing.
47	- Keep a document readable block by block: no paragraph, single list item, table cell, heading, or code line may exceed the ceiling its file records in `scripts/check-docs.mjs`. Condensing a document lowers that ceiling in the same change; raising one is a deliberate decision, not a side effect.
48	- Run `npm run check:docs` after changing a document here, adding a maintained one, or editing any of the four README pairs (the repository root and one per package) or the root contributing pair; it decides the pairing, switcher, pair-outline, relative-link, heading-anchor, index, and longest-block rules above. `node scripts/check-docs.mjs --budgets` prints the per-file longest-block table instead of deciding. The shipped core skills under `packages/agent-team/core-skills/` have their own gate, `npm run check:core-skills`. Both commands are described in [`development/README.md`](development/README.md).
49	- Commit doc changes as one Conventional Commits subject line (`docs: ...`) over only your own staged paths — never `git add -A` in the shared worktree — and run `git diff --check HEAD` before committing: the bare form inspects only unstaged work, so it passes silently once your paths are staged.
50	- `.scratch/` is work history, not an authority; move conclusions into these documents only when durable, and never rewrite archives to match new code.
51	
52	AGENTS.md files are single-language: this file and the root `AGENTS.md` are English, while maintained docs keep their `.zh.md` pairs.
53

1	# Start and checks
2	
3	English | [中文](start-and-checks.zh.md)
4	
5	## Scope
6	This document records maintenance workflows for the repository. Exact command definitions remain authoritative in the root `package.json`, package manifests, and `scripts/`; update configuration first when a command changes, then update this document.
7	
8	## Start developing
9	This repository is an independent external DSH bundle. End users install the published package; local development and real Web verification require the adjacent `../deepseek-harness` checkout.
10	
11	```text
12	../
13	├── deepseek-harness/
14	└── dsh-agent-team/
15	```
16	
17	Install dependencies with the command specified by the root README:
18	
19	```sh
20	corepack pnpm install
21	```
22	
23	`pnpm-workspace.yaml` does not declare `packages/*` as workspace members: the repository publishes one root npm package and its three `packages/*` directories are build targets of that one workspace, not independently installable packages. The file is still load-bearing — it disables automatic peer installation and carries the build-approval and release-age settings this repository relies on — so do not change or remove it because a directory lacks its own manifest. The root `node_modules` and adjacent Harness checkout provide the packages and source mappings needed for local development.
24	
25	## Verification gradient
26	Run the smallest sufficient checks for the change:
27	
28	```sh
29	npm run generate:typert
30	npm run typecheck
31	npm run check:docs
32	npm run check:core-skills
33	npm run check:boundaries
34	npm run check:versions
35	npm run check:facades
36	npm test
37	npm run build
38	npm run lint
39	npm run duplication
40	npm pack --dry-run
41	npm run check:artifact
42	npm run check:public-baseline
43	git diff --check HEAD
44	```
45	
46	Their responsibilities are:
47	
48	- `generate:typert` emits Typert Host/Remote artifacts from the Host face in `packages/agent-team/src/`.
49	- `typecheck` regenerates Typert and checks Host, tools, and Client sources.
50	- `check:docs` mechanically enforces the rules in [`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md): bilingual pairing with a working switcher, a shared heading outline per pair (the same headings at the same levels), relative links, `#fragment` heading anchors, the per-file longest-block ceiling recorded in the script, and both indexes naming exactly the documents that exist. It covers the four README pairs as well — the repository root and one per package — plus the root contributing pair, each set with its own switcher wording. Run it on its own for a documentation-only change.
51	  - `node scripts/check-docs.mjs --budgets` prints the per-file longest-block table instead of deciding.
52	- `check:core-skills` mechanically enforces the shipped skill contract under `packages/agent-team/core-skills/`: the front matter names the skill after its directory and its description names real triggers, the whole skill stays inside the reviewed budget in `scripts/check-core-skills.mjs`, every relative link stays inside the skill directory (an installer copies that directory alone), and every file under `references/` is linked from `SKILL.md`.
53	- `check:boundaries` mechanically enforces the package seams described below: no file under `packages/*/src/` may reach another package by a relative specifier that escapes its own package directory. `import type` is exempt because it is erased before runtime, and test files are out of scope because they deliberately wire directories together. Declared subpaths such as `@contexera/dsh-agent-team/remote` are the supported way to cross a seam.
54	- `check:versions` mechanically enforces the certified-version consistency rule: the CI tag, the setup tag, the development guide, the READMEs, the architecture doc, the compatibility baseline, and the bug-report placeholder must all state the same DSH baseline (in both languages). That baseline must also be the lower bound of every `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peer range. It asserts mutual agreement, never a hardcoded version, so it passes unchanged on every release lane. Run it on its own after touching any version string.
55	- `check:comments` mechanically enforces two comment rules over `packages/*/src` and `scripts/`, excluding `vendor/`. First, a per-scope comment-line budget recorded in the script (see its header). Second, a comment may not cite `.scratch/`, a work-item number, or an acceptance criterion: none of those resolve for a reader of the published package, and work history is not an authority. A bare `issue #<n>` is fine — it resolves to a real GitHub issue — and so is `Task #<n>`, a documented Team entity.
56	- `check:facades` writes nothing: it recomputes the path facades from the adjacent Harness checkout and refuses a committed `tsconfig*.json` or `.generated-harness` marker that differs from the generated output, so a subpath added to `scripts/sync-paths.mjs` cannot land without its regenerated facades. `npm test` runs it, which is why a fresh clone regenerates the facades first (see [`environments-and-install.md`](./environments-and-install.md)).
57	- `test` regenerates Typert, runs `check:facades`, `check:docs`, `check:core-skills`, `check:boundaries`, `check:versions`, and `check:comments`, then runs Vitest. `scripts/isolate-dsh-home.setup.ts` gives each test file an isolated `DSH_HOME`; tests needing a particular home must save and restore it. Startup does not prune ledger-unknown Member directories; explicit Member removal removes that Member's private memory.
58	- The suite pins one time zone (`Asia/Shanghai`, in `vitest.config.ts`), because time rendering is zone-dependent by contract: a seat states the reader's own clock, so the same expectation otherwise reads as a different hour on every runner — UTC in CI, UTC+8 where this is maintained. The pinned zone is deliberately not UTC, which keeps the assertion sharp: a formatter that reaches for `getUTCHours` renders an hour that is not the reader's and fails here. A date-sensitive test may therefore assert a literal clock time rather than read the runner's zone for its expectation.
59	- The Client bench (`packages/client-agent-team/tests/harness.tsx`) fails a spec whose rendered shipped slot entry crashed: the shipped error boundary contains the throw and reports it only through `console.error`, so an unguarded run stays green while the surface is gone. That bench also supplies what jsdom lacks (`ResizeObserver`, `document.fonts`) and the whole `conversation` service face — an absent observable member is not a missing method but a `WeakMap.set(undefined)` throw in the renderer's hook cache.
60	- `build` uses the restricted Node cleaner to clear package `lib/` directories, regenerates Typert, builds all three source trees, and uses Harness `tsdown` for the Client bundle. The published artifact remains one root npm package.
61	- `lint` runs oxlint.
62	- `duplication` runs jscpd over `packages` and `scripts` using `.jscpd.json`; treat its output as a place to look, never as a verdict, because it reports moved and restructured code as readily as copied code.
63	- `pack --dry-run` checks the root bundle's published contents; `prepack` runs the full build first, so it is a release prerequisite rather than an everyday check.
64	- `check:artifact` reads back what `npm pack` would actually ship and refuses an artifact that would ship broken: stray `.ts`/`.tsx` sources, a missing `cordis.patch.yml`, or a runtime relative import whose target is not inside the tarball. That last one is invisible to every local check, because the working tree has every file. Run it after `build` and before publishing.
65	- `check:public-baseline` compares the certified DSH baseline declared by the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peers against every public surface that restates it by hand — both READMEs and the pinned compatibility discussion in the Harness repository. A surface it cannot parse is a failure, never a skip, so rewording a README cannot quietly drop it out of coverage. It needs `gh`; `--offline` skips the discussion read and is for local iteration only.
66	
67	Both gates are publish-time checks rather than everyday ones; [`release-runbook.md`](../release-runbook.md) places them in the order a release runs them.
68	
69	Changes affecting browser bundles, Client modules, slots, Remote activation, bundle manifests, or visible UI must also run:
70	
71	```sh
72	npm run test:browser
73	```
74	
75	Visible UI changes touching Team controls or surfaces additionally run the mechanical design-language audit (shipped-reference tripwires included):
76	
77	```sh
78	node scripts/audit-ui-parity.mjs
79	```
80	
81	The audit compares Team Client CSS/TSX against the design-language contract in `docs/frontend-design/principles-and-language.md`: focus visibility, control rhythm, icon semantics, hardcoded colors, and shipped-reference presence. Run it after any visible-UI change and after every DSH upgrade.
82	
83	This builds first, copies built packages into a temporary profile, starts the official Harness Web scaffold, and runs the real journey with `/usr/bin/google-chrome` (override with `CHROME_PATH`). The sandbox setup provisions Playwright's own chromium at that path when the base image ships no browser. It cleans the temporary profile and Harness test files afterward.
84	
85	There are three explicit preview/verification paths:
86	
87	```sh
88	npm run preview:ui                         # keyless Team fixture
89	npm run test:browser                       # repeatable keyless browser acceptance
90	DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=... npm run preview       # real model interaction
91	```
92	
93	`preview` and `preview:ui` use temporary profiles and storage and clean up on `Ctrl+C`. `preview` always uses the real DeepSeek adapter and fails when credentials are missing; it does not silently switch to replay. `preview:ui` uses a keyless route-only adapter whose fixture does not call a model; an accidental model request fails explicitly.
94	
95	All three lanes stage this bundle and its declared dependency closure into a temporary profile, then name that staged copy as a profile package — the shape `dsh plugin add` leaves behind: a `file:` dependency, a link under the profile's own `node_modules`, and an entry in `dsh.profile.bundles`. The scaffold resolves plugin imports from a computed generation built out of `profile.layers`, so only a staged copy named there contributes the Team rows, and they come from the bundle's own `cordis.patch.yml`.
96	
97	A command-line overlay is not an equivalent mount. The Host row's Human-profile form is written to the profile document, and the config editor rejects that write while a later layer (a home patch or a command-line overlay) declares the same row — `overridden by a home patch or command-line overlay` — so the form stays unwritable. A staged bundle the scaffold never names resolves neither its own rows nor its dependency closure: every Team row reports `failed to import` with no module-resolution error to read, and the keyless fixture then fails on an `undefined` `ctx.agentTeam`.
98	
99	`test:browser` does not cover the two preview lanes, so boot them by hand after any change to scaffold composition or profile resolution.
100	
101	The browser journey uses a deterministic keyless Host/Client driver. It covers Agent Inbox reading/replying, Human Project and Thread navigation, persistence after reload, and restoration of the ordinary DSH surface after leaving Team mode.
102

1	# .scratch Work Rules
2	
3	This subtree holds cross-session work items: design snapshots, research, implementation tickets, prototypes, and acceptance evidence. It is not an implementation or API authority — current behavior is defined by `packages/` source and tests, and maintenance rules by [`../docs/AGENTS.md`](../docs/AGENTS.md). This file only governs how to work here.
4	
5	## Work-item structure
6	
7	Each `active/<work>/` is one directory with a short `README.md` as its single continuation entry, covering five items: status, last-checked date, current frontier (who is doing what and what is blocked), completion conditions, and the formal-doc exit.
8	
9	```
10	active/<work>/
11	├── README.md      # continuation entry (the five items above)
12	├── spec.md        # confirmed decision snapshot — written once discussion converges
13	├── issues/        # tracer-bullet implementation tickets, one file per ticket
14	│   ├── 01-<slug>.md
15	│   └── 02-<slug>.md
16	├── materials/     # research and external material (keep only what is worth re-reading)
17	└── validation/    # human-confirmed acceptance evidence (see the development doc)
18	```
19	
20	## Ticket discipline
21	
22	Each `issues/NN-<slug>.md` uses a fixed skeleton, numbered from `01` in dependency order (blockers first):
23	
24	```markdown
25	# NN — title
26	
27	**What to build:** the end-to-end behavior this ticket demonstrably delivers once done (user perspective, not a layered task list)
28	**Blocked by:** the tickets blocking it, or "None — can start immediately"
29	**Status:** pending | ready | in-progress | complete
30	
31	- [ ] acceptance criterion 1
32	- [ ] acceptance criterion 2
33	```
34	
35	- **Vertical slices**: each ticket cuts one narrow, complete path through every layer (schema → API → UI → tests), independently verifiable when done; no horizontal division of labor by layer.
36	- **Self-contained tickets**: each ticket can start in a new context without reading the whole work-item history. Avoid concrete file paths and code snippets (they go stale); exception: decision-dense fragments from prototypes (state machines, type shapes) may be inlined with their source noted.
37	- **Frontier workflow**: tickets whose blockers are all done form the frontier and are ready to start; a serial chain runs top to bottom. Tickets that are written but still carry unfinished blockers stay **pending**, so `ready` always means startable now.
38	- **Wide-refactor exception**: when one mechanical change's blast radius covers the whole repository, do not force it into a tracer bullet — order it as expand–contract: expand first (old and new coexist), migrate in batches, then contract (delete the old form).
39	
40	## Lifecycle
41	
42	- **Closing a work item**: close or delete unfinished tickets → move durable conclusions into the `../docs/` maintained documents → delete process material without provenance value → move into `archive/YYYY-MM/`.
43	- **Archive is history**: archived states and terminology only represent the working context of their time and never override current implementation; do not rewrite archives to match new code.
44	- **Transient artifacts**: logs, debug screenshots, and downloads go in `local/` or `artifacts/` (gitignored), never into active or archive.
45	
46	## Version control
47	
48	- **Active does not enter version history**: while a work item is open, its `active/<work>/` directory is gitignored working material. Force-add it (`git add -f`) only when a reviewer must see it.
49	- **Archive enters history on close**: when a work item closes, move it into `archive/YYYY-MM/` and amend that move into the commit(s) that deliver the work, so the archive records what actually shipped instead of sitting in a scratch-only commit at the tip.
50	
51	## Directory index
52	
53	See [README.md](README.md).
54

Available agent types for the Agent tool:
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)
- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)
- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)
- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

When you launch multiple agents for independent work, send them in a single message with multiple tool uses so they run concurrently.

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## deepwiki
DeepWiki MCP provides AI-powered documentation for GitHub repositories.

With a user OAuth token, all devin_* tools act in one organization: without an X-Org-Id header, the first one the user joined. Not found usually means another of their orgs; send X-Org-Id: <org id> to switch.

Available tools:
- read_wiki_structure: Get a list of documentation topics for a repository
- read_wiki_contents: View full documentation about a repository
- ask_wiki_question: Ask any question about a repository's codebase and get an AI-powered answer from its wiki
- list_wiki_repos: List the repositories that have a DeepWiki index (private mode only)
- generate_wiki: Generate a codebase wiki for a repository — only use when explicitly requested by the user (private mode only)
- devin_automation_manage: Manage Devin automations — list, get, create, update, delete, or fetch the trigger event schemas (private mode only)
- devin_billing_tag_manage: Manage Devin billing tags (groupings of Devin sessions for usage tracking) — list, get, create, assign sessions, look up session tags (private mode only)
- devin_blueprint_test: Test a candidate blueprint YAML in an authoring VM: start → run initialize → fix → run initialize again (clean VM) → run maintenance → then persist with update_environment_config (private mode only)
- devin_campaign_manage: Read and publish a bot's campaign documents (plan, readings, status) — get, update, validate (private mode only)
- devin_code_scan_manage: Manage Devin code scans, sometimes referred to as 'security scans' or 'Devin Security Swarm' — list scans, list findings, list profiles, get a profile, create a scan, remediate a finding (private mode only)
- devin_knowledge_manage: Manage Devin knowledge notes and suggestions — list, search, get, create, update, delete notes, view folder structure, list/view/dismiss knowledge suggestions (private mode only)
- devin_mcp_server_manage: Manage org MCP server installations — install (marketplace or custom), update, enable, disable, delete (private mode only)
- devin_oncall_manage: Devin Oncall operations — create and manage Oncall responders (alert, bug report and support request triage), get an Oncall report's current responder membership, page through a responder's open issues, and ingest a dashboard into Oncall knowledge (private mode only)
- devin_playbook_manage: Manage Devin playbooks — list, get, create, update, delete (private mode only)
- devin_review_manage: Trigger a Devin Review for a pull request, fetch the latest review status, or fetch a completed review's findings (private mode only)
- devin_schedule_manage: Manage scheduled Devin sessions — list, get, create, update, delete (private mode only)
- devin_session_create: Create one or more child Devin sessions (private mode only)
- devin_session_interact: Manage a Devin session — get status (one or many sessions, optionally with a short AI summary of each), send messages, sleep/terminate/archive/unarchive, read messages & attachments, manage tags (private mode only)
- devin_session_events: Inspect session events — list summaries, fetch full details, or search event contents (private mode only)
- devin_session_search: Search and filter Devin sessions (private mode only)
- devin_session_insights: Per-session cost, message counts and AI analysis (issues, action items, classification) — list, get, generate (private mode only)
- devin_user_list: List the organization's users by membership kind (direct members or IdP-group members) (private mode only)
- devin_list_integrations: List all native integrations and MCP servers with their status and settings URLs (private mode only)
- devin_find_setting: Find Devin webapp settings pages and deep-link URLs for them (private mode only)

1	# Agent 工具与上下文呈现：已确认设计
2	
3	**确认日期：2026-10-29。** Human 已确认目标、具体行为和六段完整流程；本稿将讨论整理为实施依据。同日另行授权推进实施；进度见 README。本稿不描述当前产品行为，现行行为仍以源码、测试和正式文档为准。
4	
5	## 1. 目标与范围
6	
7	首要目标是 Agent 正确理解当前状态并完成协作；其次是减少重复上下文、重复读取和无效重试。不以整体压缩比例驱动改造，不因文字缩短就判定成功。
8	
9	范围覆盖七个 Team 工具、Agent 通知、Member 动态 context、persona 与 core skills。有证据的行为问题可以修正，但行为变化与文案整理分别验证。保留七个工具的职责、权限、Attention 和 Task/Claim 语义；不改 Human Web Client 交互、不改 Harness 仓库、agent loop 或 shipped defaults。
10	
11	工程细节由实施者决定：优先复用现有能力，选能够长期保留的最简单实现，不为假设需求引入通用框架、配置开关、备用实现或独立事实数据库。
12	
13	## 2. 三个不同的状态
14	
15	| 状态 | 含义 | 不意味着什么 |
16	| --- | --- | --- |
17	| 当前上下文已提供某事实 | 来源和对象明确，必要内容完整出现在本次模型可用的上下文中 | 不等于模型理解正确，不等于持久已读 |
18	| 已确认已读 | 显式 `read` 确认的事实，由 Host 写入既有阅读状态 | 不等于事项完成，不改变 Attention |
19	| 操作已提交 | Host 按当前权限、状态及并发条件提交操作 | 不等于通知送达，不顺带清除未读 |
20	
21	收到通知、发回复、`history`、`message` 查询和自动背景补充都不主动确认已读。`read` 可以省略当前上下文里已经完整提供的正文，但必须明确确认了哪些内容、哪些正文被省略、还有多少未读。
22	
23	历史已读不会因压缩而撤销；压缩可能导致 Agent 缺少工作背景，需要重新提供。当前上下文中的完整性只是本次阅读条件的依据，不建立第二套持久未读状态。
24	
25	## 3. Member 背景与记忆
26	
27	- 新会话或上下文缺少起步背景时，提供当前身份、Project ownership、Workspace 参与及路径、预算内完整 memory 索引。
28	- 没有变化时不追加重复内容。
29	- 自己修改 `memory.md` 后，只提供简短更新提示，明确先前副本不再代表最新文件；不强迫立即读取刚写过的文件。
30	- 身份、ownership、Workspace 分别更新；ownership 和 Workspace 变化提供各自完整当前列表，包含撤销为空或从多个参与缩为一个的情况。
31	- 不因责任变化重发 memory，不因 memory 更新重发身份和 Workspace。
32	- memory 删除、不可读或超过既有预算时，明确异常及读取/维护入口，不继续把旧副本当成当前索引。
33	- 压缩后按当前实际缺失的类别补足背景；不能因为还残留一条 memory 更新提示，就假定完整索引仍在。
34	- 记忆是可能过时的参考，不覆盖 Human 输入、Workspace 指令和 Team durable facts。
35	
36	## 4. 读取与恢复讨论
37	
38	`read` 负责分批提供未读、显式确认已读，并补足必要的讨论背景；不新增由模型选择的“继续/重新进入”模式。
39	
40	- 连续讨论：新增事实全文为主，附必要回复对象和当前 Task/Claim 状态，不重复大片历史。
41	- 首次进入、压缩后背景缺失、无未读但主动查看：提供讨论主题、少量最近原文、必要引用对象和当前状态。
42	- 背景判断使用当前上下文，不用永久的“以前读过”标记。无法可靠判断时补少量背景，不默认模型记得。
43	- 背景选取使用原文和既有结构化状态；不额外调用模型生成摘要。
44	- 背景、当前状态、未读事实明确区分。背景不主动推进阅读状态，也不把 Thread card 当成已读完其 Thread。
45	- 当前批次的正文及必要回复对象优先于额外背景。未提供的历史和附件给出入口；完整消息不代表附件已读。
46	- 未读按时间顺序分批，不为了展示最新结论跳过旧的必要事实。
47	
48	### 4.1 长内容
49	
50	普通消息尽量完整返回；一批放不下就减少条数。单条本身过长时，明确分段和续读入口，不静默截断。
51	
52	完整提供之前不确认该消息已读，不凭其预览满足写入条件。`read` 续读在完整提供后确认相应消息；`message` 续读保持查询性质，之后可由 `read` 确认并省略重复正文。一次调用必须前进或明确指向可用的续读动作，不能反复返回同一开头。
53	
54	返回范围与确认范围必须来自同一次选择。不能先确认整批，再在 renderer 末尾裁掉正文。旧的“最多若干条”不能冒充总文本长度预算。具体预算在实现时按现有约定和样例测定，不新增用户配置。
55	
56	### 4.2 已提供内容的确认
57	
58	`read` 是唯一显式确认入口，不新增独立“标记已读”工具。确认当前上下文中完整可见的事实时可以不重复正文；新到的或已不完整可见的内容照常提供。无需每次回复后立刻补调用，可在处理 Inbox 时合并确认。
59	
60	## 5. 写入条件与错误恢复
61	
62	对 Thread、Main 和 Task/Claim 使用一致的“所需事实是否完整提供”原则，但不统一它们本来不同的权限或 revision 要求。Main 不因本工作项新增 Thread 写入凭据。
63	
64	可以满足相应阅读条件的内容：来源和对象明确的完整通知、`read/history/message` 结果、拒绝结果中的完整变化，以及具有必要字段的 Task/Claim 事件。只检查本次操作适用的必要事实，不要求读完全部历史。
65	
66	不能据以判定完整提供：数量、标题、摘要、截断正文、模型自己的总结或“我看过了”。看板上的当前状态只证明当前状态，不代表相关事件或讨论已提供。
67	
68	- 拒绝结果完整补齐必要事实后，允许 Agent 重新考虑并提交，不强制重复读取相同内容。
69	- 结果未补齐时，明确缺失与读取入口，不提供暗示可直接写的凭据或恢复句。
70	- 凭据不保证成功。提交时仍检查最新未读、权限、Thread revision 和 Task 状态。
71	- 仅满足写入条件不写持久已读、不消费未读标记。
72	- 不保留正文子串匹配作为备用判断。必须对应具体事实及实际可见内容，短消息不能因别处出现 `ok` 而误命中。
73	
74	## 6. 通知
75	
76	| 类型 | 默认内容 |
77	| --- | --- |
78	| 直接提及或回复通知 | 发送者、原文、所属讨论、消息定位、必要回复背景 |
79	| 普通更新 | Thread/Main 入口及未读数量，不复制正文 |
80	| Task/Claim 变化 | 操作者、对象、实际变化、变化后状态和与读者的关系；不猜原因 |
81	| ownership 变化 | 新增或撤销的责任，不顺带重发全部背景 |
82	| DM | 发送者和原文；不虚构 Thread、不计入 Inbox |
83	
84	同批合并；直接提及和责任变化优先于普通计数。重要内容被省略时明确说明还有直接信号未展开，并给入口。既有已通知正文不得反复挤占新变化；重启/恢复保留既有可重派生投递语义，不新增投递数据库。
85	
86	通知预算约束整体输出，包含外层说明和读取入口。正文截断与其完整性判断一致。已提供必要事实时，不统一追加“必须先 read”；是否需要读取按当前缺失决定。通知不确认已读。
87

1	# Package ownership
2	
3	English | [中文](package-ownership.zh.md)
4	
5	```text
6	packages/agent-team
7	  Host service + operation ledger + projections + Agent lifecycle + Remote declarations
8	        │
9	        ├── packages/tool-agent-team
10	        │     model-facing team_view / team_inbox / team_thread / team_message / team_task / team_attention / team_dm
11	        │
12	        └── packages/client-agent-team
13	              typed Remote client + Team mode + browser presentation
14	```
15	
16	These three directories are the build and export seams of one published package, `@contexera/dsh-agent-team`, declared by the root `package.json`; none has a manifest of its own. Dependency direction is one-way: Host never imports Client or tool implementation internals, tools resolve the live Host service at execution time, and Client consumes typed Remote plus public types and Harness slots — never another seam's generated `lib/` by relative path.
17	
18	[`generated-and-seams.md`](../development/generated-and-seams.md) owns the seam mechanics, the Host module layout, and the operation-extension checklist.
19	
20	- `packages/agent-team` owns Team capability. Its service keeps ledger, handles, notifications, and recovery orchestration, and its modules split as:
21	  - `src/index.ts` assembles the service and declares Remote methods;
22	  - `member-runtime.ts` owns per-Member runtime state (tool-policy restrictions, capability warnings, private skill mounts and selections, private-memory provisioning) behind a three-dependency seam (`ctx`, live member context, shared running-agents set);
23	  - `ledger.ts` commits operations;
24	  - `spec.ts` defines records;
25	  - `types.ts` re-exports the domain split (`types/entities.ts`, `types/operations.ts`, `types/requests-results.ts`) as the single public import path;
26	  - `invariant.ts` checks relationships.
27	- `packages/tool-agent-team` resolves the live Team service at execution time. It does not create another service or write projections directly.
28	- `packages/client-agent-team` has a Node half (`src/index.ts`) and browser half (`src/client/`). The browser half reads Host projections through typed Remote and renders them through public Client slots.
29	
30	A seam is earned by a second caller, a second adapter, or independently owned state — never by line count. `index.ts` and `ledger.ts` are large because they hold composition and authority, not because a layer is missing; do not split either to make a file smaller, and do not introduce `services/`, `utils/`, or `adapters/` directories before a real second implementation exists. A module that only re-exports, only forwards props, or only renames a call carries no state and no invariant: keep that call inline or delete the dead side of the contract.

1	# Tools and preset
2	
3	English | [中文](tools-and-preset.zh.md)
4	
5	The explicit `team-member` preset is the only Team Member composition. It adds coding capability rows (shell, filesystem/search, web search and fetch, background jobs, the skill loader tool, compaction), collaboration guidance/tools, Harness Workspace instruction discovery, and bounded private-memory context. Skill discovery itself is not a preset row: each Member's provider is Host-registered on its agent scope (see Host authority). Ordinary Sessions remain outside this roster and receive no Team prompt sections, tools, or Member memory.
6	
7	Every Member starts restricted to the tool definitions contributed by its selected preset, plus the explicitly shared `working_directory` tool. Host-global tools are excluded. `capabilities.tools.allow` can only narrow this baseline; it cannot authorize a Host or later plugin tool. The seven Team tools and `working_directory` remain available.
8	
9	The Host captures those definitions before Agent publication, filters request schemas during prompt assembly, and guards direct and nested execution. Later own-scope tools are hidden from requests and denied execution; replacing an allowed definition rejects request assembly and execution. Capability edits retain the original bindings. These checks apply to the exact Member, not ordinary Agents or delegated child scopes.
10	
11	Team mode does not filter prompts injected by other official or custom plugins. Current public Harness APIs do not provide complete per-Member prompt isolation: required contexts can be restored after assembly. In particular, experimental Team's `team:policy` and required `team:identity` remain visible; they do not block activation or conversation.
12	
13	This uses public Harness hooks rather than an enforced final request policy. Other assembly middleware can change the result after Team's filter. Full plugin compatibility is not certified; see [the compatibility restriction](../dsh-release-compatibility.md#37-competing-team-implementations).
14	
15	Every row `name:` is a bare specifier the Loader resolves against the profile, not against this bundle. A profile links this bundle and the host closure, so a row may name a host package or one of this bundle's own subpaths, and never a package nested inside this bundle's dependency tree. A name that resolves in a working tree can still leave the row `never started` in a real install, so a dependency's module reaches a row only through a re-export under this bundle's own name.
16	
17	The seven tools are defined in `packages/tool-agent-team/src/index.ts`; their contract is in [`tools.md`](../team-collaboration/tools.md). They mount under the isolated `team-member` preset. The Web Client is the only Human control surface and delegates every mutation through `ctx.agentTeam` typed Remote; do not restore a slash-command adapter.
18	
19	A Member has no context tool. The preset's `compaction-basic` row mounts Team's thin `member-compaction-engine` adapter: Team owns proactive admission, while the Harness's `BasicCompactionEngine` supplies the summary template, compaction transaction, and overflow recovery. [`memory-and-context.md`](../team-collaboration/memory-and-context.md) defines the budgets. Generation swaps remain Host decisions, never model ones.
20	
21	The generation swap is owned by `team-context-management.ts`, Team's own coordinator. It starts from a Host wake decision rather than a durable intent, executes through the serialized lifecycle queue, and takes the successor's identity from the retired Session so a crash converges on one successor:
22	
23	1. wait for true idle;
24	2. recheck the owned-jobs guard and the ordinary-input queue at the commit seam — a queued ordinary message defers the swap;
25	3. inside `agent.runMaintenance`, commit the idempotent `team/member-session-recycled` operation as the Host actor, recording `inputFromSeq` (the retired log's offset) when a live generation exists;
26	4. retire the old generation: its pre-step gate rejects the step without a model request, then dispose and archive (never delete); the original inbox insertions remain in the log even if already claimed;
27	5. activate the fresh Session, parented at the one it replaces;
28	6. fold the retired log from `inputFromSeq`, drop every message the successor already holds by id, deliver the rest by followup, then rederive the Inbox from the ledger.
29	
30	Maintenance is what makes the commit safe against input arriving mid-swap: the loop is parked there, so a new message waits in the durable inbox instead of reaching the generation being retired. A failed commit releases maintenance and the old generation continues; a committed one retires it, and startup or recovery finishes a swap interrupted before the replay.
31	
32	The successor first receives identity, Project ownership, Workspace participation, and its private-memory index, plus the message that woke it. Later steps append only changed or missing categories; [Member context injection](../team-collaboration/memory-and-context.md#member-context-injection) defines memory updates and recovery. There is no handoff envelope or generation announcement.
33	
34	The fold is Team's own `contextContinuity` projection unit, registered once per host at Team service init. `context-projection.ts` owns the durable checkpoint-ref naming, the Team-notice rule, the fork cut, and the folded state a generation reads back: its checkpoints with their turn-end delivery state, at most one legacy rollover intent, the continuation delivery records, and the unconsumed non-Team input the retired generation never consumed. The tool names it still decodes (`context_rollover`, `new_context`, `context_checkpoint`) are decoders for logs written by earlier builds, not tool aliases.
35	
36	`context-codec.ts` writes the one envelope this build still produces, the quiet checkpoint continuation. Recognition of that envelope, and of the two shapes earlier builds wrote, lives in `context-source.ts`; the handoff writer survives only as a test helper for those legacy shapes.
37	
38	Crash recovery is log-derived. An interrupted swap is finished from the recorded binding and the retired Session, and a legacy pending intent whose containing turn never ended durably is spent and discarded instead of leaving the generation permanently un-swappable.
39	
40	Carried-input replay is bounded and keyed by Message id. A swap records `inputFromSeq`, the retired log's offset at commit, so the fold counts only input at or after that boundary, and the retired Session's log is the only source — no message content is held in memory for the carry. A successor that already started its own turns is not skipped for that reason: the boundary and the successor's own log and inbox queues decide which messages it still lacks. Only a legacy transition without `inputFromSeq` skips the replay along its started generation.
41	
42	`agent-instructions` messages are regenerated by the successor rather than replayed as standalone turns.
43	
44	A canceled inbox splice does not identify who removed the message. Replay must preserve input cleared by disposal, so an explicit queue removal or replacement racing this swap can also be replayed. Ordinary Session cancel retains pending input by design; this limitation concerns queue editing during the transition.
45	
46	An unreadable retired previous Session fails open with a warning for two bounded classes — log corruption (`corrupt session log`, whose torn tail the Host repairs) and a deterministic released-format refusal (`SessionFormatUnsupportedError`, which no retry can change) — while missing, IO, and unknown causes stay fail-closed. A wake swap with an input boundary keeps this check even after its successor has run.
47	
48	Whether a Member Session has durable persisted content is decided through session-persistence inspection (which awaits in-flight retirement drains), never a bare metadata listing that races a suspend's final flush.
49	
50	The wake decision itself is a pure gate ladder in `wake-recycle.ts`: disabled, no prior generation, unreadable activity time, a cache possibly still warm, and a context below the waterline each answer resume, and only a cold gap over a large enough context recycles. [`memory-and-context.md`](../team-collaboration/memory-and-context.md) owns the thresholds and the configuration group.
51	
52	## Persona and core skills
53	
54	The persona is the `prefix` of the `persona` row in `cordis.patch.yml`. It is always resident and carries behavior rules, not reference material:
55	
56	- where each message belongs: Main stream post, discussion or Task start, Thread reply, or DM;
57	- that only Project owners start discussions and Tasks, and that a Task has one accountable owner;
58	- how a mention or `replyToMessageRef` differs from an ordinary message, and when to involve the Human;
59	- that naming a Member in plain prose is not a mention: `@Handle` is a delivery, so it is written only when that Member should read this Message;
60	- that accepting, closing, and reopening a Task are separate decisions, and that an Agent that executed a Task cannot accept it;
61	- etiquette, the read-before-write workflow, and a role quick reference of at most eight lines.
62	
63	Guidance is placed by use: the persona carries rules shared across tools, each tool description carries what selecting and calling that tool requires, parameter descriptions keep their required shapes, a result states this operation's state and recovery, and the bundled core skill carries detailed method and rare cases. Detail has one home; the persona keeps only the short reminder a basic call needs.
