1	# Host authority
2	
3	English | [中文](host-authority.zh.md)
4	
5	Team is one collaboration domain per DSH home. Its append-only operation ledger is durable authority for Member, Workspace, Project, Message, independent Thread aggregates, optional Task overlays, Claim, Thread Attention, Inbox, and Activity facts.
6	
7	When changing a Host capability, read package source/tests first and then the matching Harness contract. [`harness-navigation.md`](../harness-navigation.md) maps the route to `deepseek-harness/docs/subsystems/` and source packages.
8	
9	## Ledger authority and commits
10	- Current Session context may satisfy the [Thread reading requirement](../team-collaboration/boundaries.md#mutation-fences), but never confirms unread or creates another authority. Only explicit reads commit read-state changes.
11	- Agent Thread and Main stream reads add [context-aware presentation](../team-collaboration/tools.md#team_thread) to the ledger result: missing recent Message background and references to already-visible bodies. The tool selects the prefix it can render within its output ceiling, and a Thread receipt stores that bound as `selectedThroughSequence` while a legacy receipt keeps the default batch; the Host commits only that prefix. Human reads, Remote parameters, and replay semantics are otherwise unchanged, and replay never depends on a Session.
12	- Mutations enter Host authority and commit one durable operation. Projections, Inbox, tools, commands, Remote responses, and UI derive from committed operations; Client code never interprets ledger records or creates parallel authority.
13	
14	- Replay re-derives each record's expected Inbox delta and compares it exactly, so a release that changes how an existing kind is validated first records `team/rules-version-adopted` (Host actor, `{ version }`). Each record validates under the newest marker before it; a ledger with none is version 1. `initialize` appends the marker inside its own queued commit, so it precedes every later write, startup recovery included. Markers only ascend, at most one per version, and a build refuses a ledger adopted at a version above its own.
15	- Current builds implement version 2: mounting a ledger whose newest marker is lower appends the version 2 marker, and a fresh ledger records it right after `team/initialized`.
16	- Behind version 2 the Host also commits `team/main-message-posted`, `team/main-stream-read` and `team/thread-started`, which a version-1 segment rejects, while `team/message-sent` is rejected in a version-2 segment. The Host no longer writes `team/message-sent` (a Thread starts with `startThread`); it replays only inside version-1 segments.
17	- An inbox delta may carry an optional `mainMarkers` list with its own marker shape (`projectRef` plus a `messageRef` or `activityRef`). It appears only when it changes something, so version-1 records keep their stored bytes, and a departing Member's Main stream markers clear in the same operation as its other inbox state.
18	- An inbox delta may also carry an optional `mainAttention` list (`set` of Main stream Attention rows, `removed` of their keys), with the same "only when it changes something" rule, so every delta written before Main stream Attention existed keeps its stored bytes. `team/main-attention-changed` is the kind that writes it; its row is keyed by Member × Project and never enters a Thread index.
19	- An Attention row carries the `source` that established it: `thread-author`, `claim`, `accountable`, `project-owner`, `mention`, or `self`. It is optional in storage, so rows written before it existed keep their bytes.
20	- On load, a missing cause is derived from the operation that wrote the row: an ownership grant reads as `project-owner`, a Claim as `claim`, a Thread start as `thread-author`, a transfer or reopen as `accountable`, and a legacy read inherits the existing Attention row's cause. The repaired row then participates in strict replay validation, so old records keep their stored shape without weakening the comparison.
21	- An Agent is woken from its Main stream markers through the same direct-notification path as a Thread marker, and an ordinary Main stream update its Attention covers is delivered immediately. Every unread fact interrupts, so an ordinary Thread update reaches a reader only because it follows that Thread: no identity — owner or accountable — sits in a slower class, and nothing accumulates a count first. `covered` is the process-memory signature that stops an unchanged rederivation spending a second attempt; a queued but unread notice is replaced, not stacked.
22	- A reply records the Message it answers as `replyToMessageRef` on the Message itself, and the Host resolves that ref against the ledger before committing: an unknown ref, or one belonging to another Thread, is refused rather than stored.
23	- The parent's author joins the recipients at commit and takes a direct marker exactly as a mention does — the same resolution, the same markers, no invitation step. Under rules version 2 `undeliveredMentions` is never populated: every addressable recipient is delivered, whether or not the Thread ever carried it, and nothing follows as a side effect. Reporting an undelivered remainder is the version-1 compatibility path alone.
24	- The quoted picture — the parent's author and one line of its body — is a read-time derivation (`replyTo`), never a second stored copy. It therefore cannot disagree with the parent and still fills in when the parent sits outside the page being read. A ref that no longer resolves stays a bare ref. Quoting is not optional: the parameter is part of the reply contract, and a reply carrying a ref is accepted or refused on the ref alone.
25	
26	## Lifecycle and notifications
27	- Agent lifecycle, JSON/SQLite replay, authorization, idempotency, and revision checks stay on Host. Durable unread changes may produce one bounded coalesced Agent context notification through the public safe boundary: direct mentions carry their Message and source, Task/Claim Activities carry the complete event (actor, object, Claim refs or transfer endpoints), and ordinary unread carries only a body-free Thread-first route. Promotion is a Task activity and reaches followers through Activity markers. Notifications are not a second authority and do not promise exactly-once processing.
28	- The notice ranks missing direct signals before reminders and ordinary counts; [attention-and-messaging.md](../team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.md) owns its order, caps, and character budget.
29	- A committed Session transition (`team/member-session-renewed`, `team/member-session-rolled-over`, `team/member-session-recycled`) records the desired binding, not a completed one: retiring the old generation and activating the target are Host effects outside the ledger write. Startup and the explicit Member recovery action both finish an interrupted transition from the recorded previous Session, and each effect derives its own completion — a live handle never proves the archive half ran. A repeated request answers with the recorded receipt and an honest status, never a second binding.
30	- Every durable Member state has one desired external effect set — the [Member Lifecycle](../domain-model.md#member-lifecycle) table. Each lifecycle operation re-runs that set right after its commit, and startup re-runs it for every non-enabled Member, so an archive, suspension, or removal interrupted by a crash or a failed Workspace/Session/filesystem call converges by repeating the same derivation rather than by a second durable write.
31	- Startup never activates a non-enabled Member: an effect that fails during startup is logged and retried at the next boot instead of failing the boot. Lifecycle operations for one Member stay serialized in submission order, while different Members never queue behind each other's waits.
32	- Task reminders are Host-owned `team/reminder-raised` operations evaluated after Team events, never timers. Their optional `reminderMarkers` Inbox delta is private to one recipient; replay retains the complete episode for deduplication after its marker is consumed.
33	- Reminder operations invalidate the Task Thread change scope so the Human Inbox refreshes, but add no public fact or revision. Acceptance, close, and lifecycle cleanup remove obsolete unread markers while retaining episode history. Agent idle observations are process-local, retained across generation replacement and discarded on Host restart; unknown idle never satisfies a time condition.
34	
35	- After the ledger append, delivery effects follow — commit listeners, Client change invalidation, the participation notice, and one wake per affected Member. Each runs in a boundary that logs a failure instead of failing the operation, so a failed listener or wake still answers with the committed result, not a false rollback; only invariant divergence still rejects. A failed Inbox wake clears its recorded notice state, so the next commit touching that Member rederives the same durable Inbox facts and retries without a second append. DM keeps its explicit recorded-but-not-delivered error.
36	
37	## Which operations wake a Member, and how recovery is chosen
38	
39	A wake is one bounded coalesced notice the Host delivers over one of four causes, each carrying the durable fact that produced it:
40	
41	| Cause | What produced it |
42	| --- | --- |
43	| `commit` | any committed operation touching the Member: a mention, a DM, a Task activity, a promotion, an accepted answer |
44	| `transition` | a recorded `team/member-session-renewed`, `team/member-session-recycled`, or legacy `team/member-session-rolled-over` whose retire and activation effects complete out of order; the rederived Inbox is sequenced after any carried input |
45	| `activation` | a fresh activation, carrying the previous Session id when input was carried forward |
46	| `running` | the Member's own `agent/status` going `running` — one wake per transition, not per step |
47	
48	Waking is not a second authority and never promises exactly-once model processing. A wake that fails delivery clears its recorded notice state, so the next commit touching that Member rederives the same durable facts and retries without a second append.
49	
50	`recoverMember` is the manual path and picks exactly one of these, in order:
51	
52	| Condition | Action | Use it when |
53	| --- | --- | --- |
54	| handle absent, or the live handle's Session id is not the recorded binding, and a recorded transition exists | finish the recorded transition | a crash or a failed effect left a Session transition half-applied |
55	| durable state is not `enabled` but a live handle survives | finish that state's effects | a suspend, archive, or removal committed but its disposal failed |
56	| a live handle whose preset composition is gone | reactivate in place | a reload lost the preset composition, so the Member's tools are unavailable |
57	| no live handle at all | reactivate | the activation itself failed |
58	| otherwise | steer a resume prompt | the Member is alive, composed, and bound — every other state has already been handled |
59	
60	An error-state Member with a live handle is the last row: `recoverMember` steers it, and a cause that is still present makes the next turn fail again. Distinguish the two before choosing: a broken model route or a rejecting gateway is fixed by changing the route, not by recovering the Member, and steering recovers nothing until the route answers. Recovery never resets a context generation: a stranded Member whose binding already moved finishes that recorded transition, and nothing in the Remote surface renews or rolls a Session over.
61	
62	A Member's current failure reason is carried on its status as a `diagnostic` and rendered by the Client. It is derived from the live surface, not persisted: after a Host restart it is re-derived only if something wakes the Member, so an un-woken Member shows no reason until the next operation touches it.
63	
64	## Projections and the change stream
65	- The `contextContinuity` unit folds live Session events through the Harness projection registry. It retains only the legacy intent, checkpoint, continuation and unanswered-input facts needed for recovery; activation and retired-Session recovery can also fold an inspected log in full.
66	- The Member clock baseline uses `session-event-cursor.ts` to consume only appended events. The cursor restarts when the Session identity, inherited prefix, length or anchor event changes. Its guard relies on the append-only log contract; an in-place replacement with the same sequence and event type is not detected.
67	- `changes()` is a streaming Remote with one optional scope (workspace/project/thread/presence); an omitted scope observes shared Team projection changes, not presence. Host registers the listener before emitting the current baseline, then emits matching invalidations, retaining only the latest pending version while a consumer pauses. Cancellation or Host disposal closes the subscription.
68	- Thread reads and `team/dm-sent` change no shared projection, so neither advances its version nor wakes subscribers. A private reminder does invalidate its Task Thread scope: that is how an open Human Inbox learns about it, without turning it into public Thread history.
69	
70	  Presence uses a process-local epoch; other scopes report the latest shared-projection ledger sequence. Versions are meaningful only within their scope and Host lifetime. Host recomputes Inbox hints only for Members affected by an operation.
71	- `TeamChangeStream` shares one logical stream per scope within each page through `ctx.remote.$stream()`; Harness owns the shared `/api/remote.mux` WebSocket and connection recovery. Each new baseline, including an unchanged or lower version after reconnection, requests a fresh Host read. This closes the initial-read race and recovers failed reads without a new commit. The last listener leaving disposes that scope; plugin disposal closes all scopes. Carrier failures are reported once until recovery; terminal failures are reported without a Team-owned retry loop.
72	
73	  Team has no long-poll fallback, cross-page leader election, or single-active-page restriction. Concurrent supplemental reads coalesce notifications and retain a trailing read when another notification arrives during a fetch, rather than suppressing reconnect baselines by an old version. The Human Inbox badge subscribes without a scope, debounces Inbox totals, and also refreshes after local Thread reads. Presence subscriptions update Member availability without waking the Inbox. Notifications are invalidation hints, never a second facts store.
74	- Read projections are bounded by purpose. `view` answers the requested fact page plus the Thread it names: its catalog fields carry that page's Tasks, Threads, display ordinals and Claims. Only `includeCatalog` returns the Task/Thread/Claim catalog of the whole request scope — the address-book projection the model-facing `team_view` renders.
75	- A page read walks the fact ledger until one match past its limit; a catalog read adds one directory filter over the Threads in scope plus one live-Claim lookup per Task row. Those are the components to report separately, never as one total: a returned row count alone does not show what a read walked.
76	- Claims are bucketed per Task by a replay-derived index, so a per-Task read — a Claim list, a Thread picture, an Inbox row, the Task board — never walks the ledger's whole Claim set. Every index here is rebuilt by replay, never a second durable authority.
77	
78	## Session persistence and replay
79	- The bundle targets DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` and uses the current DSH Session persistence: the shipped JSONL backend migrates released historical formats itself (v0/v1/v2 → V3 → V4), and old-format Session data needs no manual disposal. Team nevertheless retains a narrow replay normalization for old pre-Message `occurredAt` records, and exactly one record shape still reaches it: the pre-receipt `team/thread-read` snapshot, which froze Message anchors and Thread facts beside the Inbox delta it consumed.
80	
81	  That is the only Thread-read form that stores an instant at all — the receipt every current read writes carries progress and its Inbox delta only — and it is normalized and validated in place, never rewritten. Do not add Team Session migration, broad compatibility reads, or fallback storage paths.
82	
83	## Attention and Inbox authority
84	- Thread Attention is private Member × Thread state. The Host is the only Inbox authority. Session history may retain bounded notification context but never a parallel unread projection.
85	- The Inbox read ranks the reader's whole unread queue, then materializes preview text, the instant's person and live Claim owners only for the rows it returns; its totals stay whole-queue, so a one-row badge still reports every unread Thread. `threadObservations` returns the newest `limit` observations with `hasMore`, and its follower set is always the complete current state.
86	
87	## Sessions, policy, and context pressure
88	- Team-managed Agent sessions use the explicit Team preset and trusted `danger-full-access` policy. An untitled Member session receives its handle as a title; explicit or previous titles win.
89	- Member context is owned by two Host-side mechanisms and no model tool (see Tools and preset): Team controls request budgets through its preset adapter over the Harness's `BasicCompactionEngine`, which shortens an oversized Session in place, and the generation coordinator swaps a cold Session at a wake boundary, recording `team/member-session-recycled` as the Host actor. [`memory-and-context.md`](../team-collaboration/memory-and-context.md) owns the pressure and wake thresholds.
90	- A swapping generation reports unavailable with a `rollover` diagnostic until its successor activates, so a Client following the row never opens a Session that does not exist yet.
91	- A swap carries input, not context: the commit records the retired log's offset and the successor replays only the input at or after it, deduplicated by Message id, using the original durable inbox insertions even for already-claimed input. Nothing is copied through process memory (see [Tools and preset](tools-and-preset.md)).
92	- Pending/error bookkeeping is process-local; only compactions in a transaction add Session history.
93	- Terminal recovery classifies each `agent/error` from structured Harness data before any wording. The stable code decides alone — `RATE_LIMIT` is rate limiting, `TRANSPORT`/`TIMEOUT` a transient network failure, an explicit 429/503 response rate limiting — and any other code (quota, auth, context, request) stays manual whatever its message says. Only a codeless error falls back to the narrow message signatures.
94	- `agent/error` owns terminal recovery with its consecutive-error limit, and the failure keeps its recorded Member diagnostic.
95	- A Team wake discarded before any `turn/start` is the one error diagnostic with no `agent/error` behind it. A Team-owned Inbox or recovery notice that leaves the queue before the turn opens, and that the Host did not replace or dispose, records a `runtime` diagnostic with `source: 'agent/inbox/discarded'`, the `sessionId`, and `occurredAt`. A notice the Host replaces or disposes raises nothing, so ordinary replacement never errors. Like every runtime diagnostic it is process-local, re-derived only on the next wake.
96	
97	## Private memory, archival, and identity effects
98	- The Member preset derives identity, Project ownership, Workspace participation, and private-memory context from current Host facts and the current Session surface. Classification and memory-update rules are defined in [Member context injection](../team-collaboration/memory-and-context.md#member-context-injection); this creates no second durable state store.
99	- Private-memory directories under `$DSH_HOME/agent-team/members/` are Host-owned effects of Member identity. Activation ensures the directory, `notes/`, and missing `memory.md`; startup does not prune unknown directories. Explicit removal archives the Session and removes that Member's private directory; unrelated entries remain untouched.
100	
101	  Both that removal and the activation-time rename of a pre-fix colon directory are confined to the running process's own members root. The recorded `privateMemoryPath` is a durable absolute fact that names a directory in whichever DSH home added the Member, so a process resolving another home refuses to move or delete it (with a warning) instead of taking the Member's real private memory out of its home.
102	- Member and Project archival is the reversible third state between suspend and remove. `archiveMember` commits `team/member-archived`, disposes the live session (private memory and the Session log stay on disk), archives the Session from grouping surfaces, and releases the Member's active Claims with public `claims_released` Activities plus Attention/marker cleanup. A hidden Member must not leave Tasks stuck in progress or phantom unread counts.
103	
104	  `archiveProject` commits `team/project-archived` with the same release shape across every owner on the Project's Threads; Memberships survive both archival forms (hidden state, not departure).
105	
106	  Archived entities are gone from every Team API surface — projections (view projects/threads/tasks/members, mention candidates, Project joins, edits), ref resolution (`resolveTaskRefs`/`resolveThreadRefs` skip them so message bodies render plain text), and ref-addressed reads (`readThread`/`threadHistory`/`threadObservations`/`listClaims` reject with an explicit archived error, never an unknown-ref disguise). The facts stay complete in the ledger for replay and a future restore, and that boundary is the archival-vs-remove divide.
107	
108	  Removal from archived stays available as the data hygiene path, and there is deliberately no restore entry point this round (mirroring archived dsh sessions). Ledgers written before Project archival omit `project.state`; the record schema normalizes it to `active` at load.
109	
110	## Member capabilities and skills
111	- Member capabilities (`capabilities` on the Member entity: reserved `tools.allow`, `skills.allow`) are durable intent carried verbatim by every lifecycle operation. Committing performs no known-name validation so old ledgers stay replayable across Harness upgrades; divergence is derived at activation as non-persisted `capabilityWarnings`. `tools.allow` is a deliberate interface reservation: it has no UI write path today.
112	
113	  Edits follow the partial-update semantics of `model`: an omitted field keeps the stored value and an explicit `null` clears it, so a caller that does not manage capabilities can leave the field out and any Remote-written override survives.
114	- Activation restricts every Member before preset validation (mount → restrict → validate), even without `tools.allow`. The allow-list can only narrow the preset baseline, retaining the seven Team tools and `working_directory`; names outside that baseline drop with a warning. Tool filtering, execution checks, and their limits are defined in [Tools and preset](tools-and-preset.md).
115	
116	  Editing the allow-list on a live Member swaps the restriction at a turn boundary in the same Session: idle Members apply immediately, and a running Member's edit waits for that Member's turn to end. Each Member owns one lifecycle chain, so the wait holds only that Member's later operations, still in submission order, while managing another Member never queues behind it and the ledger keeps its single ordered writer.
117	
118	  Host shutdown releases every pending wait instead of waiting out a turn that may never end, and a Session disposed outside the chain also releases it. A stop cancels that Member's in-flight turn and then waits for the Agent to quiesce, so a stop queued behind a parked edit reaches the boundary after that edit has applied and then usually finds the Agent idle. A stop never clears or aborts a committed configuration: the edit either applies at the boundary or reports `deferred:no-live-handle`, and either order leaves the stored intent in force at the next activation.
119	
120	  Waits are logged by class with their Member, Session, and duration: `stage 'wait-turn'` for waiting on the Member's own turn, and `stage 'wait-external'` for external execution such as the Agent releasing its Session write path. Restriction failures during activation surface as that Member's activation failure.
121	- A failed live apply never widens the surface: the edit keeps its ledger commit, the previous restriction stays in force (restored when the new one fails to install), the Remote call surfaces the failure, and retrying the same request re-applies the stored configuration without a second commit. The Host compares stored intent against the capability effects the runtime has actually applied, never against the requesting call's own history.
122	- Configuration edits report their effect separately from their commit: `updateMember` returns `effect` as `applied`, `already-applied`, `deferred:no-live-handle`, or `deferred:generation-changed` (saved now, applied at the next activation). A failure never appears as a value — it stays a rejection and is also kept as a routable `capability-apply` diagnostic whose `detail` carries requestId, operationId, stage, and reason with the Session in `sessionId`, logged under the same correlation group.
123	- Every roster row carries `capabilityState` (`applied` | `pending`), derived from the effects the runtime actually applied; states with no live surface report `pending` literally. The field is orthogonal to `availability`/`presence`: those answer whether the Member runs, this answers whether its stored configuration is in effect.
124	- Skills are Member-private. The preset carries no shared skill-filesystem row; instead the Host registers one filesystem provider per Member on that agent's exact scope layer (the traceable-service seam, same shape as the tool restriction). That provider scans exactly two Team-owned roots with default roots excluded: the plugin's bundled read-only core skills (`packages/agent-team/core-skills/`, first — a same-name bundled skill stays stable across upgrades) and the Member's writable `$DSH_HOME/agent-team/members/<memberId>/skills/`.
125	
126	  A Member catalog therefore starts with the bundled set (the `member-skill-manager` meta skill, which owns all skill craft guidance — the persona itself only states the private-space physical facts). Installing is writing into the Member's own directory (directory form `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with optional references/scripts, or a flat `.md`), there is deliberately no upload Remote, and the filesystem watcher feeds discovery.
127	
128	  `skills.allow` filters `list()` output through a live selection swap on the mounted provider (edits swap the filter and invalidate the catalog at the same turn boundary as tool edits); filtering is a visibility semantic, not a security boundary — both roots stay scanned and watched. Member removal deletes the private directory with its skills; suspend/resume and Host restart restore the identical catalog.
129	
130	## Host service surface (`ctx.agentTeam`)
131	
132	The Host row publishes one service, `ctx.agentTeam`, consumed in two distinct ways with different stability promises. There is no CLI, no `bin`, and no loopback HTTP entry: the Web Client is the only Human control surface, and every change reaches the Host through the typed Remote.
133	
134	- **Remote methods** (the `@Remote`-decorated ones, e.g. `members`, `view`, `addMember`, `updateMember`, `sendMessage`, `readThread`, `inbox`, `humanProfile`) are the Client contract. They are typed through Typert artefacts generated from the declarations, so the Client, the model-facing tools, and any other consumer compile against the same shape; changing one is a contract change.
135	- **Host-only service methods** (e.g. `memberForAgent`, `membersForClient`, `status`, and the activation/lifecycle internals) exist for in-process Host callers — the preset row, commit listeners, and startup derivation. They carry no compatibility promise and may move between releases.
136	
137	Only the Remote set is a contract. Everything else on `ctx.agentTeam` is internal and may change shape without a migration note.
138	
139	A preset row must resolve `ctx.agentTeam` while it runs, never capture it statically at declaration time: the service is provided when the Host plugin starts, so a row that closed over it at import time sees nothing. The same applies to `ctx.get('agentTeam')` in external code, which is undocumented use of an internal surface rather than a supported integration point.
140	
141	## Composer attachments (cache, not archive)
142	
143	Attachments live in the bounded cache `$DSH_HOME/agent-team/attachments/v1/<attachmentId>/`, with a sanitized original name and `meta.json`; they are never ledger bytes or an archive. `putAttachment` enforces a 10 MB file cap and sanitizes names; `getAttachment` serves Client display. Messages record metadata while the stored body contains machine-facing `[attachment] <absolute path>` lines. The Client strips those lines and renders thumbnails/chips.
144	
145	The request's `requestId` is an upload's idempotency key. Retrying the same payload replays the original result instead of writing a second entry, reusing that key for a different payload is refused as a request collision, and the cache id derives from the request id alone. A retry therefore converges on the same entry after a Host restart without a second durable store or an in-memory map.
146	
147	The Project and Thread composers accept files both through the "+" picker and by pasting into the draft; a paste that carries files is intercepted and joins the same pending-file chips, while plain-text pastes keep their native insertion.
148	
149	Garbage collection runs at startup and every 24 hours: referenced uploads older than 72 hours and orphaned uploads older than 24 hours are removed, while metadata remains. Agent-sent absolute paths are validated as absolute non-empty regular files under 10 MB and rejected atomically if any path fails; each surviving path is copied into an immutable cache entry whose id derives from the message or reply request and the path's position in it. A manually pasted absolute path is simply read by the Agent; Host touches nothing it does not own.
150	
151	That request-derived identity is what makes retries cheap: a repeated send or reply converges on the entry the first attempt prepared instead of writing an orphan, so the stored body — one `[attachment]` line per file — stays identical across retries. A message or reply that fails after preparation removes the entries this attempt prepared which no committed Message references, with the ledger's reference set as the guard; genuinely unreferenced uploads stay GC's to reclaim.
152	
153	On a reused request id the ledger compares the recorded resolved attachment ids with the retry's resolved ids, so a retry carrying a different attachment set is refused as a collision.
154	
155	## Human profile and version footnote
156	
157	The Human's display name and avatar reference live in the Team Host row's own Config, in the settings namespace `wowyuarm-agent-team-host` (user layer); avatar bytes live in the persistent `$DSH_HOME/agent-team/human/v1/` store, never in the TTL-bound attachment cache.
158	
159	The retired `agent-team-human` section is no longer an authority: the rc.1 settings importer carries sections across through a closed built-in mapping, so a third-party section stays behind in the renamed legacy document. A boot that finds the row still pristine — the default name and no avatar — adopts those facts through the same write path the settings page uses, and anything already re-entered wins.
160	
161	Four typed Remotes serve the settings page: `humanProfile` (name, avatar reference, and version footnote facts) and `putHumanAvatar`/`getHumanAvatar`/`removeHumanAvatar` (images only, 10 MB cap shared with attachments; a removed entry throws and the Client falls back to the initial).
162	
163	The footnote carries the version of the bundle this Host runs from — read from the installed package's own manifest, so it states what the profile actually installed rather than a string every release must remember to bump — plus the repository link and an update tip. The tip names the newer version once a background check has observed a newer published release.
164	
165	The check asks the public npm `latest` document at most every 12 hours, refreshes in the background so profile reads never wait on the network, settles every failure as "no update known", and stays off while `DSH_AGENT_TEAM_UPDATE_CHECK=0`.
166	
167	The ledger reads the same profile for `team_view` and @ matching, so a rename reaches every surface at once. `human` stays a permanent alias for the Human and no agent handle may claim the literal, so `@human` keeps delivering across renames while chips render the current display name.
168

    24	/** Rebuild the exact Host Activity fact a view came from; a view missing its identity yields none, so it can never bind. */
    25	export function activityFromView(value: ActivityViewFields, projectRef?: string): ActivityFact | undefined {
    26	  if (value.kind !== 'activity' || value.activityRef === undefined || value.actor === undefined || value.activity === undefined) return undefined
    27	  const base = { activityRef: value.activityRef, sequence: value.sequence, actor: value.actor }
    28	  if (projectRef !== undefined) {
    29	    if (value.memberId === undefined || (value.activity !== 'owner-added' && value.activity !== 'owner-removed')) return undefined

    31	  }
    32	  if (value.threadRef === undefined || value.taskRef === undefined) return undefined
    33	  const thread = { ...base, taskRef: value.taskRef, threadRef: value.threadRef }

    36	    case 'done':
    37	    case 'release':

    39	        : activityFact({ ...thread, kind: value.activity, claimRef: value.claimRef } as unknown as AgentTeamActivity)

    46	    case 'reopen':
    47	    case 'transfer':
    48	      return activityFact({ ...thread, kind: value.activity, from: value.from, to: value.to,
    49	        releasedClaimRefs: value.releasedClaimRefs === undefined ? undefined : [...value.releasedClaimRefs],
    50	        completedClaimRefs: value.completedClaimRefs === undefined ? undefined : [...value.completedClaimRefs],
    51	        acceptedClaimRefs: value.acceptedClaimRefs === undefined ? undefined : [...value.acceptedClaimRefs],
    52	        refollowedMembers: value.refollowedMembers === undefined ? undefined : [...value.refollowedMembers] } as unknown as AgentTeamActivity)
    53	    default:

    55	  }

docs/architecture/tools-and-preset.md:34:The fold is Team's own `contextContinuity` projection unit, registered once per host at Team service init. `context-projection.ts` owns the durable checkpoint-ref naming, the Team-notice rule, the fork cut, and the folded state a generation reads back: its checkpoints with their turn-end delivery state, at most one legacy rollover intent, the continuation delivery records, and the unconsumed non-Team input the retired generation never consumed. The tool names it still decodes (`context_rollover`, `new_context`, `context_checkpoint`) are decoders for logs written by earlier builds, not tool aliases.
docs/architecture/tools-and-preset.md:36:`context-codec.ts` writes the one envelope this build still produces, the quiet checkpoint continuation. Recognition of that envelope, and of the two shapes earlier builds wrote, lives in `context-source.ts`; the handoff writer survives only as a test helper for those legacy shapes.
docs/frontend-design/components.md:14:Anchored at the row's own top edge, the card hangs beside the author line, so the room between its lower edge and the first words is the row's top padding plus that author line minus the card's own height — 3px at the default content size, and it keeps clear as the content font axis grows. A continuation row has no author line to hang beside, so its card rises over its run's own previous line — the words those actions belong to — and still clears the first line it acts on.
docs/frontend-design/components.md:29:A run groups consecutive same-sender Messages and its Thread entry row. Activity and unread boundaries break runs. An entry row in a grouped row gets a hairline; ordinary continuation does not. Runs have no hover box, fill, shadow, or permanent border—only two-pixel spacing. Time is stated by the row that owns it, never by a line: a row with an identity line states its instant beside the name, a continuation row in the avatar seat under the pointer or keyboard focus.
docs/frontend-design/refresh-copy-accessibility.md:8:Thread passive changes merge into current facts; the durable read pointer advances automatically on open and on every arrival (a bounded read's remainder drains through the serial continuation loop), and `newFactsCount` only drives the pure jump hint. `loadOlder` has concurrency protection.
docs/development/environments-and-install.md:45:**CI lanes. ** [`.github/workflows/ci.yml`](../../.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs typecheck plus the full test suite on clean `ubuntu-latest` and `windows-latest` runners — on pull requests, pushes to `master`, and manual `workflow_dispatch`. Both lanes execute the same six-step environment contract above; the Windows lane runs every step through git bash (`shell: bash`) because the default pwsh breaks backslash line continuations, and links the harness packages through directory junctions so no symlink privilege is needed.
docs/architecture/tools-and-preset.zh.md:34:折叠是 Team 自己的 `contextContinuity` projection unit，在 Team service init 时按 host 注册一次。`context-projection.ts` 拥有 durable checkpoint ref 命名、Team notice 规则、fork cut，以及一代读回的那份折叠状态：带 turn-end 投递状态的 checkpoints、至多一条 legacy rollover 意图、continuation 投递记录，以及被退役那代从未消费的非 Team 输入。它仍然解码的工具名（`context_rollover`、`new_context`、`context_checkpoint`）是给早先版本日志用的解码器，不是 tool alias。
docs/architecture/tools-and-preset.zh.md:36:`context-codec.ts` 只写当前构建还产出的那一个信封：quiet checkpoint continuation。识别它、以及识别早先版本写下的两种形状，都在 `context-source.ts`；handoff 的写者只作为那些 legacy 形状的测试 helper 保留。
docs/frontend-design/thread-and-composer.md:14:A Message leads with its author: the avatar seat and, beside it, the author name and the time. The seat is `--team-identity-seat` (34px) and is the single place the face's size is stated — the initial avatar and the uploaded-image avatar both take their width and height from it, the continuation row's time centres inside it, and the two hairlines that hug the text column are inset past it, so changing the face needs no second edit. It is declared on the shared conversation surface rather than the Thread page, because the Project feed renders the same Message rows.
docs/frontend-design/thread-and-composer.md:20:A continuation row has no identity line; its time rides in the avatar seat as described under [Timeline scrolling](#timeline-scrolling).
docs/frontend-design/thread-and-composer.md:67:Every Thread has one entry in the Project feed, drawn as a single quiet row under its anchor Message's body that both states and opens the Thread. It never treats Task as a navigation level, and no state of an entry ever lives on the identity line. A continuation row in a run has no identity of its own, so a cluster parked there would float alone at a line's far end. Any placement that far right costs the reader a trip across the column for the value they came for.
docs/architecture/host-authority.zh.md:11:- Agent 的 Thread 与 Main stream read 在 ledger 结果上增加[按上下文调整的呈现](../team-collaboration/tools.zh.md#team_thread)：缺失的近期 Message 背景与已可见正文的省略说明。工具按输出上限选出能渲染的前缀，Thread receipt 以 `selectedThroughSequence` 记录这个界限，旧 receipt 仍按缺省 batch 解释；Host 只提交该前缀。Human read、Remote 参数与 replay 语义均不变，重放不依赖 Session。
docs/architecture/host-authority.zh.md:64:- `contextContinuity` unit 经 Harness projection registry 增量折叠活动 Session 事件，只保留恢复所需的旧 intent、checkpoint、continuation 与未答复输入。激活与退休 Session 恢复也可全量折叠被检视日志。
docs/frontend-design/layout-and-typography.md:47:Message time comes from Host projection and shares the ledger operation instant. Consecutive same-sender messages form a run, and time is stated by the row itself: beside the name where the row has an identity line, in the avatar seat under the pointer where it is a continuation. A day boundary gets a centered date anchor, and the Project feed alone draws a `TeamRunDivider` hairline at a five-minute boundary, with no instant on it. `team-separators.ts` is the single authority for both decisions.
docs/frontend-design/layout-and-typography.md:51:The seat is 34px and neither clips nor grows, so it states the time of day alone (`formatClockTime`). The dated forms measure 57px within the year and 87px across it — wide enough to paint over the words beside them. A run breaks at every calendar-day change, so a continuation always shares its run head's day and the date is already one row up. The exact instant stays on the label's `title` (`formatAbsoluteTime`), as the Inbox row and the Project entry line do.
docs/team-collaboration/memory-and-context.zh.md:59:对于可恢复的临时 service errors，Host 按 Member 的连续 `agent/error` occurrences 计数。计数依据不是 recovery wakeups 或 error text。前两次 errors 各自在延迟后 wake 一次。第 3 次立即停止自动 recovery，并保留 error 交给 operator。不同 recoverable kinds 不中断连续 error 的计数。只有 clean turn end 清零，non-recoverable error 取消 tracking。Recovery notice 自带合并内容：continuation 与当前 durable Inbox facts。所以 ordinary Inbox notification 不会覆盖 Recovery notice，也不会追加第二条提示。
docs/team-collaboration/tools.zh.md:15:cursor 只延续 Thread 行。continuation 页只渲染 Threads。翻页可达全部获授权的顶层 Threads，含 taskless 与不在首页的 taskful。页脚把 cursor 称为 Thread cursor，说明是否还有更旧的 Thread anchors。
docs/team-collaboration/tools.zh.md:29:Thread 的选择界限是持久的：receipt 存储 `selectedThroughSequence`，replay 据此重建同一次确认，界限之后的 facts 保持未读。相同重试只返回该 receipt 与当前未读画面，不会再次确认。写入该字段之前的 receipt 仍按缺省 batch 解释。Human 的读取、Remote 参数与读取语义都不变。
docs/team-collaboration/tools.zh.md:68:history 页渲染历史结果与 Thread 身份。首页给 full anchor，continuation 页给 bounded subject。渲染选中的 facts、该 sequence 窗口内的派生 Task 卡与 cursor/hasMore 页脚，绝无当前 Claims 或上下文建议。每条 activity fact 都只从该事件本身得出结构：activity ref、actor、Task 与 Thread refs，以及这条 activity 记录的 Claim refs 或 transfer 两端。绝不是裸 kind，也不用当前 Task/Claim 状态补历史。当一次 `read` 确认的是一个仍处于 done 状态 Task 的未读验收时，这些事实就写在 facts 里，read 不对读取者的上下文给出任何建议：没有 rollover 工具，也没有代际选择，就没有动作可陈述。
docs/architecture/host-authority.md:11:- Agent Thread and Main stream reads add [context-aware presentation](../team-collaboration/tools.md#team_thread) to the ledger result: missing recent Message background and references to already-visible bodies. The tool selects the prefix it can render within its output ceiling, and a Thread receipt stores that bound as `selectedThroughSequence` while a legacy receipt keeps the default batch; the Host commits only that prefix. Human reads, Remote parameters, and replay semantics are otherwise unchanged, and replay never depends on a Session.
